1416-
1417--- We've seen two different ways of expressing logical claims
1418--- in Lean: with booleans (of type `Bool`), and with
1419--- propositions (of type `Prop`).
1420-
1421--- Here are the key differences between `Bool` and `Prop`:
1422-
1423--- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00):
1424---     Check formatting:
1425-
1426--- - ⠀
1427--- - `Bool`
1428--- - `Prop`
1429--- - decidable?
1430--- - yes
1431--- - no
1432--- - useable with `match`?
1433--- - yes
1434--- - no
1435--- - works with `rewrite` tactic?
1436--- - no
1437--- - yes
1438-
1439--- The crucial difference between the two worlds is
1440--- decidability. Every (closed) Lean expression of type `Bool`
1441--- can be simplified in a finite number of steps to either
1442--- `true` or `false` — i.e., there is a terminating mechanical
1443--- procedure for deciding whether or not it is true.
1444-
1445--- This means that, for example, the type `Nat → Bool` is
1446--- inhabited only by functions that, given a `Nat`, always
1447--- yield either `true` or `false` in finite time; and this, in
1448--- turn, means (by a standard computability argument) that
1449--- there is no function in `Nat → Bool` that checks whether a
1450--- given number is the code of a terminating Turing machine.
1451-
1452--- By contrast, the type `Prop` includes both decidable and
1453--- undecidable mathematical propositions; in particular, the
1454--- type `Nat → Prop` does contain functions representing
1455--- properties like "the nth Turing machine halts." The second
1456--- row in the table follows directly from this essential
1457--- difference. To evaluate a pattern match (or conditional) on
1458--- a boolean, we need to know whether the scrutinee evaluates
1459--- to `true` or `false`; this only works for `Bool`, not
1460--- `Prop`.
1461-
1462--- The third row highlights an important practical difference:
1463--- equality functions like `Nat.beq` that return a boolean
1464--- cannot be used directly to justify rewriting with the
1465--- rewrite tactic; propositional equality is required for this.
1466--- Since `Prop` includes both decidable and undecidable
1467--- properties, we have two options when we want to formalize a
1468--- property that happens to be decidable: we can express it
1469--- either as a boolean computation or as a function into Prop.
1470-
1471--- As an example, we can write
1472-
1473-example : Nat.even 42 := rfl
1474-
1475--- or that there exists some `k` such that `42 = double k`.
1476-
1477-example : Nat.Even 42 := by exists 21
1478-
1479--- Of course, it would be deeply strange if these two
1480--- characterizations of evenness did not describe the same set
1481--- of natural numbers!
1482-
1483--- Fortunately, they do! To prove this, we first need two
1484--- helper lemmas.
1485-
1486-theorem even_double (k : Nat) : Nat.even (Nat.double k) = true := by
1487-  induction k with
1488-  | zero =>
1489-    rewrite [Nat.double_zero, Nat.even_zero]
1490-    rfl
1491-  | succ n ih =>
1492-    rewrite [Nat.double_succ, Nat.even_succ, Nat.even_succ, Bool.not_not]
1493-    exact ih
1494-
1495--- ### Exercise (3 stars): even_double_exists ⭐⭐⭐
1496-
1497-theorem even_double_exists (n : Nat) :
1498-    ∃ (k : Nat), n = bif Nat.even n then Nat.double k else Nat.double k + 1 := by sorry
1499-
1500--- Now the main theorem:
1501-
1502-theorem even_iff_Even {n : Nat} : Nat.even n = true ↔ Nat.Even n where
1503-  mp h := by
1504-    have ⟨k, hk⟩ := even_double_exists n
1505-    rewrite [h, cond_true] at hk
1506-    subst hk
1507-    exists k
1508-  mpr h := by
1509-    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := h
1510-    subst hk
1511-    exact even_double k
1512-
1513--- In view of this theorem, we can say that the boolean
1514--- computation `n.even` is reflected in the truth of the
1515--- proposition `∃ (k : Nat), n = k.double`.
1516-
1517--- Similarly, to state that two numbers n and m are equal, we
1518--- can say either
1519-
1520--- - that `n == m` returns `true`, or
1521--- - that `n = m`
1522-
1523--- Again, these two notions are equivalent:
1524-

1526---     This proof is from the typeclass version, which makes
1527---     more sense if maps are included — CGH

1529-example (n₁ n₂ : Nat) : n₁ == n₂ ↔ n₁ = n₂ := beq_iff_eq

1531--- So what should we do in situations where some claim could be
1532--- formalized as either a proposition or a boolean computation?
1533--- Which should we choose?
1534-
1535--- In general, both can be useful. Which we choose has to do
1536--- with the *computational* nature of Lean's core language,
1537--- which is designed so that every function it expresses is
1538--- total, and by default computable unless we explicit indicate
1539--- otherwise. As an example, consider trying to write a
1540--- function `α → α → Bool` checking for equality on an
1541--- arbitrary type:

1573---

1588--- is the way that we express in Lean that a given proposition

1596--- Now we are able to complete such proofs by computation using
1597--- the `decide` tactic:

1599-example : Nat.Even 2 := by decide
1600-example : Nat.Even 4 := by decide
1601-example : Nat.Even 6 := by decide
1602-example : Nat.Even 100 := by decide

1604-example : ∀ n < 10, Nat.Even (2 * n) := by decide

1607--- In general, Lean will try to use typeclass synthesis with
1608--- `Decidable` in order to determine when it is appropriate to
1609--- use `Prop` and `Bool` interchangeably. For instance, while
1610--- our example `eq` failed above while trying to use
1611--- propositional equality `=` in the condition of an `if`
1612--- statement, we are allowed to write

1614-def nat_eq (m n : Nat) : Bool := if m = n then true else false
1615-
1616--- Why is this allowed? It is precisely because equality of
1617--- natural numbers is decidable, and Lean makes use of this
1618--- fact. If we print this definition with notation unset, we
1619--- would find that it is using `instDecidableEqNat`
1620-
1621-set_option pp.all true in
1622-#print nat_eq

1624--- which proves that this equality is decidable.

1626--- This is only half the story however: while Lean's core
1627--- theory enables this computation, Lean is also often used in
1628--- applications where we don't care about computability, such
1629--- as pure mathematics. In particular, it is possible to write
1630--- a function for arbitrary equality:
1631-
1632-sf_experiment
1633-  open scoped Classical in
1634-  noncomputable def eq {α : Type} (a₁ a₂ : α) := if a₁ = a₂ then true else false

1637-  #print eq

1639--- But we have indicated to Lean, using the `noncomputable`
1640--- keyword and `Classical` namespace, that we are *not*
1641--- interested in computation. What is happening in the
1642--- background is that this allows typeclass synthesis to find
1643--- the scoped instance `Classical.propDecidable`, which makes
1644--- use of the axiom of choice to provide a proof that all
1645--- propositions are *classically* decidable. This sort of
1646--- definition is suitable for use with proofs, but is not
1647--- allowed to be used in conjunction with computational
1648--- features of Lean such as the `decide` tactic or the `#eval`
1649--- command.

11--- Copied from `SubVerso.Compat` to avoid making generated projects depend on verso.
12--- We want to have info state and messages available right after the elaboration,
13--- so we need to disable `Elab.async` which would let diagnostics produced asynchronously
14--- through spanshot tasks.
15-private def commandWithoutAsync (act : CommandElabM Unit) : CommandElabM Unit := do
16-  match (← get).scopes with
17-  | [] => act
18-  | h :: t =>
19-    let mut orig : Option Bool := none
20-    try
21-      orig := h.opts.get? `Elab.async
22-      modify fun s => { s with scopes := { h with opts := h.opts.setBool `Elab.async false } :: t }
23-      act
24-    finally
25-      if let h :: t := (← get).scopes then
26-        let opts := orig.map (h.opts.setBool `Elab.async) |>.getD (h.opts.erase `Elab.async)
27-        modify fun s => { s with scopes := { h with opts := opts } :: t }
28-
29-private def withRestoringState (keepMsgs : Bool) (m : CommandElabM Unit) : CommandElabM Unit := do
30-  let savedState ← get
31-  try
32-    m
33-  finally
34-    let state ← get
35-    set { savedState with
36-      -- Preserve the info tree
37-      infoState := state.infoState
38-      messages := if keepMsgs then state.messages else savedState.messages }

40-namespace IndentedCommands
41-
42-/-! # Block Commands Parser
43-  Parse an indented command block. Commands are separated by new lines.
44-  Since we want to capture parsing errors in `sf_expect_failure`,
45-  we can't use Lean command parser directly in our command's syntax,
46-  because any parsing error occurred would fail `sf_expect_failure` itself.
47-  One possible solution is to first parse the whole indented body as raw syntax,
48-  and then run Lean's command parser followed by command elaboration.
49--/
50-
51-open Parser
52-
53-private def rawLineEndFn : ParserFn :=
54-  eoiFn <|> satisfyFn (· == '\n') "line break"
55-
56-/-- Consumes everything until the next newline and then consumes the newline itself. -/
57-private def rawLineFn : ParserFn :=
58-  takeUntilFn (· == '\n') >> rawLineEndFn
59-
60-/- For each line after the first body line, consumes leading whitespaces.
61-  If it's blank, consumes the newline; otherwise consumes the line
62-  requiring the indentation.
63--/
64-private def rawIndentedLineFn : ParserFn := atomicFn <|
65-  takeWhileFn (· == ' ') >>
66-  (satisfyFn (· == '\n') "line break" <|>
67-    (checkColGeFn "indented command sequence" >> rawLineFn))
68-
69-private def rawCommandBlockFn : ParserFn :=
70-  rawFn (rawLineFn >> manyFn rawIndentedLineFn) (trailingWs := true)
71-
72-private def rawCommandBlock : Parser := { fn := rawCommandBlockFn }
73-
74-@[combinator_parenthesizer rawCommandBlock]
75-private def rawCommandBlock.parenthesizer := PrettyPrinter.Parenthesizer.visitToken
76-
77-@[combinator_formatter rawCommandBlock]
78-private def rawCommandBlock.formatter := PrettyPrinter.Formatter.visitAtom Name.anonymous
79-
80-private partial def runRawCmdsAux
81-    (ictx : InputContext) (pstate : ModuleParserState) : CommandElabM Unit := do
82-  let state ← get
83-  let scope := state.scopes.head!
84-  let pctx :=  {
85-      env := state.env
86-      options := scope.opts
87-      currNamespace := scope.currNamespace
88-      openDecls := scope.openDecls : ParserModuleContext
89-    }
90-  let (cmd, pstate, messages) := parseCommand ictx pctx pstate state.messages
91-  modify fun state => { state with messages }
92-  unless cmd.isOfKind ``Command.eoi do
93-    elabCommand cmd
94-    runLinters cmd
95-    unless isTerminalCommand cmd do
96-      runRawCmdsAux ictx pstate
97-
98-/- Recovers the source info and elaborates the commands -/
99-private def runRawCmds (body : Syntax) : CommandElabM Unit := do
100-  let some source := body.getSubstring? (withLeading := false) (withTrailing := false)
101-    | throwErrorAt body "command sequence has no source range"
102-  let fileName ← getFileName
103-  let fileMap ← getFileMap
104-  -- Recall that `rawIndentedLineFn` may consume whitespaces after the newline.
105-  -- Here we move the ending back to the last non-whitespace character to produce
106-  -- correctly positioned diagnostics.
107-  let stopPos := source.trimRight.stopPos
108-  if h : stopPos ≤ fileMap.source.rawEndPos then
109-    let ictx := InputContext.mk fileMap.source fileName
110-      (fileMap := fileMap) (endPos := stopPos) (endPos_valid := h)
111-    runRawCmdsAux ictx { pos := source.startPos, recovering := false, hasLeading := false }
112-  else
113-    throwErrorAt body "invalid command-sequence source range"
114-
115-end IndentedCommands
116-
117-end
118-
119-public meta section
120-
121-open Parser IndentedCommands
122-
123-/--
124-Elaborates the enclosed commands and reports their diagnostics,
125-but discards their effects afterwards.

127-Example:
128-```lean
129-sf_experiment
130-  def hidden : Nat := 1
131-  #check hidden
132--- `hidden` is not available here.
133-```
134--/
135-def experimentTk := leading_parser
136-  "sf_experiment"
137-
138-@[command_parser] def experimentCmd := leading_parser
139-  experimentTk >> checkLinebreakBefore "indented command sequence" >>
140-    checkColGt "indented command sequence" >> withPosition rawCommandBlock

SFLCompat/Recall/Check.lean

1-module
2-
3--- For testing cases in this file
4-meta import all Init.Prelude
5-public meta import SFLCompat.Recall.Common
6-
7-/-!
8-# Recall, checked by elaboration
9-
10-`sf_recall` lets a chapter restate a definition from earlier in the
11-development while the build checks that the restatement means the same
12-thing. The restated declaration is elaborated for real, inside a hidden
13-namespace, and compared with the original up to definitional equality; the
14-temporary declaration is then rolled back.
15-
16-Two forms:
17-
18-```
19-sf_recall
20-  def twice (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat := f <| f n
21-
22-sf_recall statement twice_id : twice id 3 = 3
23-```
24-
25-What is compared:
26-
27-* types, always;
28-* a `def`'s value, safety, and abbreviation status;
29-* an inductive's constructors, one by one (names, parameter and index
30-  counts, and each constructor's type);
31-* a structure's fields, field defaults, and type-class registration;
32-* a theorem's statement, never its proof.
33-
34-So a recalled definition may be reformatted or rephrased into something
35-definitionally equal, and a theorem may be reproved differently or, with
36-the `statement` form, restated without any proof. The command is global and
37-available wherever this module is imported.
38--/
39-
40-
41-namespace SFLCompat.Recall.Check
42-
43-open Lean Elab Command Meta
44-
45-meta section
46-
47-structure DeclId where
48-  /-- This could be a private name. -/
49-  actual : Name
50-  display : Name
51-
52-def DeclId.ofActual (actual : Name) : DeclId :=
53-  { actual, display := privateToUserName actual }
54-
55-/-- Look up the actual name in temp elaboration namespace -/
56-def tempDeclId (userName : Name) : CommandElabM DeclId := do
57-  let env ← getEnv
58-  let privateName := mkPrivateName env userName
59-  let actual ←
60-    if env.contains privateName then pure privateName
61-    else if env.contains userName then pure userName
62-    else throwError "the re-elaborated declaration '{userName}' was not found"
63-  return .ofActual actual
64-
65-def renameBackName (chk orig n : Name) : Name :=
66-  if chk.isPrefixOf n then n.replacePrefix chk orig
67-  else
68-    let chk := privateToUserName chk
69-    if chk.isPrefixOf n then n.replacePrefix chk orig else n
70-
71-/--
72-Replaces the name prefix `chk` with `orig` in every constant that `e`
73-mentions: `chk` itself becomes `orig`, and a longer name such as a hidden
74-constructor `chk.mk` becomes `orig.mk`. Constructor types mention the
75-hidden inductive type's name in argument and resulting positions, so this
76-rewrite is what makes a re-elaborated declaration comparable with the
77-original.
78--/
79-def renameBack (chk orig : DeclId) (e : Expr) : Expr :=
80-  e.replace fun
81-    | .const n us =>
82-      let n' := renameBackName chk.actual orig.actual n
83-      if n == n' then none else some (.const n' us)
84-    | _ => none
85-
86-/--
87-Applies `renameBack` to the expressions recorded in an info tree. The info
88-recorded while elaborating the hidden copy mentions the hidden constants,
89-so hovers over a recalled declaration would otherwise display the hidden
90-names; rewriting before the trees are stored makes them display the
91-originals, which also exist after the hidden copy is rolled back.
92--/
93-partial def renameBackInfoTree (chk orig : DeclId) (t : InfoTree) : InfoTree :=
94-  match t with
95-  | .context (.parentDeclCtx n) t' =>
96-    .context (.parentDeclCtx (renameBackName chk.actual orig.actual n))
97-      (renameBackInfoTree chk orig t')
98-  | .context ctx t' => .context ctx (renameBackInfoTree chk orig t')
99-  | .node i children =>
100-    let i := match i with
101-      | .ofTermInfo ti => .ofTermInfo (reTerm ti)
102-      | .ofDelabTermInfo dti => .ofDelabTermInfo { dti with toTermInfo := reTerm dti.toTermInfo }
103-      | other => other
104-    .node i (children.map (renameBackInfoTree chk orig))
105-  | .hole m => .hole m
106-where
107-  reTerm (ti : TermInfo) : TermInfo :=
108-    { ti with
109-      expr := renameBack chk orig ti.expr
110-      expectedType? := ti.expectedType?.map (renameBack chk orig) }
111-
112-/--
113-Checks that the types of the original constant `x` and its re-elaborated
114-counterpart `chk` agree, definitionally. The restated type is first
115-rewritten by `renameBack renChk renOrig`; the defaults compare a
116-declaration against its own hidden copy, and the constructor check
117-overrides them with the enclosing inductive types, whose names the
118-constructor types mention. The restatement's universe parameters are
119-instantiated with the original's.
120--/
121-def checkTypesMatch (x chk : DeclId) (ref : Syntax)
122-    (renChk : DeclId := chk) (renOrig : DeclId := x) (hint : MessageData := .nil) :
123-    TermElabM Unit := do
124-  let origInfo ← getConstInfo x.actual
125-  let chkInfo ← getConstInfo chk.actual
126-  unless origInfo.levelParams.length == chkInfo.levelParams.length do
127-    throwErrorAt ref (m!"universe parameters of '{x.display}' do not match" ++ hint)
128-  let chkType := (renameBack renChk renOrig chkInfo.type).instantiateLevelParams
129-    chkInfo.levelParams (origInfo.levelParams.map .param)
130-  unless ← isDefEq chkType origInfo.type do
131-    throwErrorAt ref
132-      (m!"the statement of '{x.display}' does not match.\n\
133-          Original:{indentD origInfo.type}\nRestated:{indentD chkType}" ++ hint)
134-
135-/--
136-All constructor syntax nodes of a command, in source order: an inductive
137-type's `| name : ...` alternatives and a structure's `name ::` header.
138--/
139-partial def ctorStxs (stx : Syntax) : Array Syntax :=
140-  let inner := stx.getArgs.flatMap ctorStxs
141-  if stx.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.ctor
142-      || stx.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.structCtor then
143-    #[stx] ++ inner
144-  else inner
145-
146-/-- Does the syntax contain a doc comment? -/
147-def hasDocComment (stx : Syntax) : Bool :=
148-  (stx.find? (·.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.docComment)).isSome
149-
150-/--
151-Suggestions localized to a mismatched constructor, returned as a pair of
152-hints for name errors and for type errors. An inductive type's `| name : ...` alternative is replaced
153-with the original constructor's own source. A structure's `name ::` header
154-can carry a name fix but not a field fix, so its type errors keep `outer`,
155-the suggestion that replaces the whole restatement. A constructor without
156-syntax also falls back to `outer`.
157--/
158-def ctorHints (ctorRef : Syntax) (origCtor origShort : Name) (outer : MessageData) :
159-    TermElabM (MessageData × MessageData) := do
160-  try
161-    if ctorRef.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.ctor then
162-      let origSrc := dedent (← sourceOf origCtor)
163-      -- A restatement without a doc comment gets a suggestion without one;
164-      -- the meaning check does not compare documentation.
165-      let origSrc := if hasDocComment ctorRef then origSrc
166-        else stripLeadingComments origSrc
167-      let restatedSrc ← sourceOfSyntax ctorRef
168-      let h ← replaceWithOriginalHint ctorRef origSrc restatedSrc
169-      return (h, h)
170-    if ctorRef.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.structCtor then
171-      let restatedSrc ← sourceOfSyntax ctorRef
172-      let h ← replaceWithOriginalHint ctorRef s!"{origShort} ::" restatedSrc
173-      return (h, outer)
174-    return (outer, outer)
175-  catch _ => return (outer, outer)
176-
177-/--
178-Checks a re-elaborated declaration against the original, definitionally.
179-Errors point at `ref`, the restated command, except for constructor
180-mismatches, which point at the offending constructor within it.
181--/
182-def checkMatch (x chk : DeclId) (ref : Syntax) (hint : MessageData := .nil) :
183-    TermElabM Unit := do
184-  checkTypesMatch x chk ref (hint := hint)
185-  let origInfo ← getConstInfo x.actual
186-  let chkInfo ← getConstInfo chk.actual
187-  match origInfo, chkInfo with
188-  | .defnInfo orig, .defnInfo restated =>
189-    let chkVal := (renameBack chk x restated.value).instantiateLevelParams
190-      restated.levelParams (orig.levelParams.map .param)
191-    unless ← isDefEq chkVal orig.value do
192-      throwErrorAt ref
193-        (m!"the value of '{x.display}' does not match.\n\
194-            Original:{indentD orig.value}\nRestated:{indentD chkVal}" ++ hint)
195-  | .inductInfo orig, .inductInfo restated =>
196-    unless orig.numParams == restated.numParams && orig.numIndices == restated.numIndices do
197-      throwErrorAt ref (m!"parameters or indices of '{x.display}' do not match" ++ hint)
198-    unless orig.ctors.length == restated.ctors.length do
199-      throwErrorAt ref
200-        (m!"'{x.display}' has {orig.ctors.length} constructors, \
201-            the restatement has {restated.ctors.length}" ++ hint)
202-    -- A `structure` that writes no `name ::` header has a constructor
203-    -- without syntax; the whole command remains the fallback position.
204-    let ctorRefs := ctorStxs ref
205-    let mut i := 0
206-    for origCtorActual in orig.ctors, chkCtorActual in restated.ctors do
207-      let origCtor := DeclId.ofActual origCtorActual
208-      let chkCtor := DeclId.ofActual chkCtorActual
209-      let ctorRef := ctorRefs[i]?.getD ref
210-      let origShort := origCtor.actual.replacePrefix x.actual .anonymous
211-      let (nameHint, typeHint) ← ctorHints ctorRef origCtor.actual origShort hint
212-      let renamedChkCtor := DeclId.ofActual <|
213-        chkCtor.actual.replacePrefix chk.actual x.actual
214-      unless origCtor.actual == renamedChkCtor.actual do
215-        throwErrorAt ctorRef
216-          (m!"constructor '{renamedChkCtor.display}' does not match \
217-              '{origCtor.display}'" ++ nameHint)
218-      checkTypesMatch origCtor chkCtor ctorRef (renChk := chk) (renOrig := x) (hint := typeHint)
219-      i := i + 1
220-    -- A structure's field names are part of its interface, and the
221-    -- constructor's type does not record them, so they are compared
222-    -- through the environment's structure information.
223-    let env ← getEnv
224-    match getStructureInfo? env x.actual, getStructureInfo? env chk.actual with
225-    | some origSi, some chkSi =>
226-      let origFields := origSi.fieldNames.map DeclId.ofActual
227-      let chkFields := chkSi.fieldNames.map DeclId.ofActual
228-      unless origFields.map (·.actual) == chkFields.map (·.actual) do
229-        throwErrorAt ref
230-          (m!"the fields of '{x.display}' do not match.\n\
231-              Original:{indentD (toMessageData (origFields.map (·.display)).toList)}\n\
232-              Restated:{indentD (toMessageData (chkFields.map (·.display)).toList)}" ++ hint)
233-      unless getOutParamPositions? env x.actual == getOutParamPositions? env chk.actual
234-          && getOutLevelParamPositions? env x.actual == getOutLevelParamPositions? env chk.actual do
235-        throwErrorAt ref (m!"the type-class metadata of '{x.display}' does not match" ++ hint)
236-    | some _, none =>
237-      throwErrorAt ref (m!"'{x.display}' is a structure, but the restatement is not" ++ hint)
238-    | none, some _ =>
239-      throwErrorAt ref (m!"'{x.display}' is not a structure, but the restatement is one" ++ hint)
240-    | none, none => pure ()
241-  -- A theorem's proof is not compared; restating it as a `def` is also
242-  -- accepted, since only the statement matters.
243-  | .thmInfo _, .thmInfo _ => pure ()
244-  | .thmInfo _, .defnInfo _ => pure ()
245-  | .axiomInfo _, .axiomInfo _ => pure ()
246-  | .opaqueInfo _, .opaqueInfo _ => pure ()
247-  | _, _ =>
248-    throwErrorAt ref
249-      (m!"'{x.display}' and its restatement are different kinds of declaration" ++ hint)
250-
251-/--
252-`sf_recall` restates a definition from earlier in the development and checks
253-that the restatement means the same thing. `sf_recall statement x : T` checks
254-that `T` matches the statement of the theorem `x`.
255--/
256-syntax (name := recallChk) "sf_recall " command : command
257-
258-@[inherit_doc recallChk]
259-syntax (name := recallChkStmt) "sf_recall " &"statement " ident " : " term : command
260-
261-elab_rules : command
262-  | `(sf_recall $cmd:command) => do
263-    let decl ← declaredName cmd
264-    let xActual ← liftCoreM <| withoutExporting <|
265-      realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo decl.ident
266-    let x := DeclId.ofActual xActual
267-    -- The restatement elaborates unchanged inside a fresh hidden namespace:
268-    -- self-references (an inductive's own name in its constructor types, in
269-    -- resulting-type position included) resolve to the hidden copy, and
270-    -- every other name resolves as it would at the recall site. The
271-    -- namespace comes from the name generator: `_uniq` names cannot be
272-    -- written in source, so it is collision-free, and unlike a macro-scoped
273-    -- name it is an ordinary component, so declarations under it keep the
274-    -- prefix structure that `renameBack` and the constructor comparison
275-    -- rely on.
276-    let ns ← liftCoreM (mkFreshId : CoreM Name)
277-    -- Any mismatch gets a clickable fix: replace the restatement with the
278-    -- original's source text, indented like the restatement. The helpers
279-    -- for recovering and re-indenting source are shared with the
280-    -- byte-for-byte variant.
281-    -- A failed hint must not fail the check: not every constant has a
282-    -- declaration range or sources on the search path.
283-    let hint ←
284-      try
285-        let original := dedent (← sourceOf x.actual)
286-        let original := if hasDocComment cmd then original
287-          else stripLeadingComments original
288-        let restated ← sourceOfSyntax cmd
289-        liftCoreM <| replaceWithOriginalHint cmd original restated
290-      catch _ => pure .nil
291-    let envBefore ← getEnv
292-    try
293-      let chk ← withScope (fun sc => { sc with currNamespace := sc.currNamespace ++ ns }) do
294-        let saved ← getResetInfoTrees
295-        try
296-          elabCommand cmd
297-          -- this could be a private name
298-          let userName := (← getScope).currNamespace ++ decl.written
299-          let chk ← tempDeclId userName
300-          let inner ← getResetInfoTrees
301-          modifyInfoState fun s => { s with trees := saved ++ inner.map (renameBackInfoTree chk x) }
302-          return chk
303-        catch e =>
304-          let inner ← getResetInfoTrees
305-          modifyInfoState fun s => { s with trees := saved ++ inner }
306-          throw e
307-      runTermElabM fun _ => checkMatch x chk cmd (hint := hint)
308-    finally
309-      setEnv envBefore
310-  | `(sf_recall statement $ident:ident : $stmt:term) => do
311-    let xActual ← liftCoreM <| withoutExporting <|
312-      realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo ident
313-    let x := DeclId.ofActual xActual
314-    addConstInfo ident x.actual
315-    let region := mkNullNode #[ident.raw, stmt.raw]
316-    let restated ← sourceOfSyntax region
317-    runTermElabM fun _ => do
318-      -- The suggestion restates the original's type as the pretty-printer
319-      -- renders it. The statement cannot be carved out of the original's
320-      -- source, since finding its boundary would require parsing the
321-      -- source in the elaboration context of its declaration site.
322-      let hint ←
323-        try
324-          let origInfo ← getConstInfo x.actual
325-          let printed ← ppExpr origInfo.type
326-          replaceWithOriginalHint region
327-            s!"{ident.getId} : {printed}" restated
328-        catch _ => pure .nil
329-      let t ← Term.elabType stmt
330-      Term.synthesizeSyntheticMVarsNoPostponing
331-      -- Remaining level metavariables become parameters, so the restatement
332-      -- must carry as many universe parameters as the original; comparing
333-      -- against fresh level metavariables instead would let a fixed
334-      -- universe pass for a polymorphic original.
335-      let t ← instantiateMVars (← Term.levelMVarToParam t)
336-      let origInfo ← getConstInfo x.actual
337-      let stParams := (collectLevelParams {} t).params
338-      unless stParams.size == origInfo.levelParams.length do
339-        throwErrorAt stmt
340-          (m!"universe parameters of '{x.display}' do not match" ++ hint)
341-      let t := t.instantiateLevelParams stParams.toList
342-        (origInfo.levelParams.map .param)
343-      unless ← isDefEq t origInfo.type do
344-        throwErrorAt stmt
345-          (m!"the restated statement of '{x.display}' does not match.\n\
346-              Original:{indentD origInfo.type}\nRestated:{indentD t}" ++ hint)
347-
348-end
349-namespace Tests
350-
351-sf_recall
352-  inductive Nat where
353-  | zero
354-  | succ (n : Nat) : Nat
355-
356--- A constructor mismatch is reported at the offending constructor, not at
357--- the whole restatement.
358-/--
359-@ +4:2...26
360-error: the statement of 'Nat.succ' does not match.
361-Original:
362-  Nat → Nat
363-Restated:
364-  Nat → Nat → Nat
365-
366-Hint: Replace the restatement with the original:
367-  | succ (̲n̲ ̲: N̲a̲t̲)̲ ̲:̲ ̲Nat ̵→̵ ̵N̵a̵t̵ ̵→̵ ̵N̵a̵t̵
368--/
369-#guard_msgs (positions := true) in
370-sf_recall
371-  inductive Nat where
372-  | zero
373-  | succ : Nat → Nat → Nat
374-

376-  | red | green | blue
377-

381-
382-sf_recall
383-  inductive Palette where
384-    | red | green | blue

386--- A misnamed constructor's suggestion replaces just that constructor.
387-/--
388-@ +3:18...24
389-error: constructor 'SFLCompat.Recall.Check.Tests.Palette.blau' does not match 'SFLCompat.Recall.Check.Tests.Palette.blue'
390-
391-Hint: Replace the restatement with the original:
392-  | b̵l̵a̵u̵b̲l̲u̲e̲
393--/
394-#guard_msgs (positions := true) in
395-sf_recall
396-  inductive Palette where

399--- Definitionally equal reformulations are accepted.
400-sf_recall
401-  def twice (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat := f <| f n

406-sf_recall statement Nat.add_comm : ∀ (n m : Nat), n + m = m + n

409--- becomes a parameter and matches, and a fixed universe is rejected.
410-theorem poly_refl.{u} : ∀ {α : Sort u} (a : α), a = a := fun _ => rfl
411-

413-

417-Hint: Replace the restatement with the original:

419--/

455-  [fst, snd]

1-module
2-
3-public meta import Lean.Elab.Command
4-
5-namespace SFLCompat.Recall
6-
7-open Lean Elab Command
8-public meta section
9-
10-/-- All `declId` nodes in a command, in source order. -/
11-partial def declIds (stx : Syntax) : Array Syntax :=
12-  let inner := stx.getArgs.flatMap declIds
13-  if stx.isOfKind ``Lean.Parser.Command.declId then #[stx] ++ inner else inner
14-
15-/-- The syntax and written name of the single declaration in a recall command. -/
16-structure DeclSyntax where
17-  ident : Syntax
18-  written : Name
19-
20-/--
21-The `declId` node of a declaration command, together with the name written
22-in it. A command that declares several names (a `mutual` block) or none (an
23-anonymous `instance`, an `example`) is rejected.
24--/
25-def declaredName (cmd : Syntax) : CommandElabM DeclSyntax := do
26-  let defined := declIds cmd
27-  match h : defined.size with
28-  | 0 => throwErrorAt cmd "the restated command does not declare a name"
29-  | 1 =>
30-    let declId := defined[0]
31-    return { ident := declId[0], written := declId[0].getId }
32-  | n + 2 =>
33-    for h : i in 0...(n + 1) do
34-      logErrorAt defined[i]
35-        "the restated command declares several names; recall one declaration at a time"
36-    throwErrorAt defined[n + 1]
37-      "the restated command declares several names; recall one declaration at a time"
38-
39-/--
40-Removes the block indentation of a declaration's source text. The first
41-line starts at the declaration's first token and has no indentation of its
42-own; each following line is stripped of the smallest indentation found
43-among the non-blank ones. Restatements of the same text at different block
44-depths dedent to identical strings, and every other difference survives
45-dedenting.
46--/
47-def dedent (s : String) : String :=
48-  match indentWidth s, s.splitOn "\n" with
49-  | some n, first :: rest =>
50-    "\n".intercalate (first :: rest.map (fun l => String.ofList (l.toList.drop n)))
51-  | _, _ => s
52-where
53-  /-- The smallest indentation among the non-blank continuation lines. -/
54-  indentWidth (s : String) : Option Nat :=
55-    s.splitOn "\n" |>.drop 1 |>.map (·.toList)
56-      |>.filter (fun l => !l.all (·.isWhitespace))
57-      |>.map (fun l => (l.takeWhile (· == ' ')).length)
58-      |>.min?
59-
60-/--
61-Indents the continuation lines of dedented source text by `n` spaces, so
62-that the text reads correctly at the block depth of a restatement.
63--/
64-def reindent (s : String) (n : Nat) : String :=
65-  match s.splitOn "\n" with
66-  | [] => s
67-  | first :: rest =>
68-    let pad := String.ofList (List.replicate n ' ')
69-    "\n".intercalate (first :: rest.map fun l =>
70-      if l.toList.all (·.isWhitespace) then l else pad ++ l)
71-
72-/--
73-Removes the comments from the front of dedented source text, together with
74-the whitespace around them, so that a suggestion offered for a restatement
75-that carries no comments does not introduce any. The text of a declaration
76-or of a constructor begins with its doc comment when it has one, possibly
77-accompanied by ordinary comments, and a leading block comment ends at its
78-depth-balanced closing delimiter, so a character scan recognizes the
79-leading run of comments exactly. A comment elsewhere in the text cannot be
80-recognized without lexing and is left in place.
81--/
82-def stripLeadingComments (s : String) : String := Id.run do
83-  let mut cs := s.toList.dropWhile (·.isWhitespace)
84-  repeat
85-    if cs.take 2 == ['/', '-'] then
86-      cs := cs.drop 2
87-      let mut depth := 1
88-      while depth > 0 do
89-        match cs with
90-        | [] => return s
91-        | '/' :: '-' :: rest => depth := depth + 1; cs := rest
92-        | '-' :: '/' :: rest => depth := depth - 1; cs := rest
93-        | _ :: rest => cs := rest
94-    else if cs.take 2 == ['-', '-'] then
95-      cs := cs.dropWhile (· != '\n')
96-    else
97-      break
98-    cs := cs.dropWhile (·.isWhitespace)
99-  return String.ofList cs
100-
101-/--
102-A clickable suggestion that replaces the restated text at `span` with
103-`original`, which must already be dedented. The original's indentation is
104-moved to match the restatement's: the restatement's own indentation width
105-when it has continuation lines, one step past the span's start column when
106-it does not.
107--/
108-def replaceWithOriginalHint [Monad m] [MonadFileMap m] [MonadLiftT CoreM m]
109-    (span : Syntax) (original restated : String) : m MessageData := do
110-  let fileMap ← getFileMap
111-  let k := match dedent.indentWidth restated, span.getRange? with
112-    | some k, _ => k
113-    | none, some r => (fileMap.toPosition r.start).column + 2
114-    | none, none => 2
115-  MessageData.hint m!"Replace the restatement with the original:"
116-    #[{ suggestion := .string (reindent original k), span? := some span }]
117-
118-/--
119-The source text of the declaration of `x`, from the file that declared it.
120-
121-The location comes from the declaration range that Lean records for every
122-constant. A declaration from the current file is read out of the file map;
123-one from an imported module is read from its source file, found on the
124-source search path. In a book build the whole project's sources are on that
125-path, so definitions can be recalled across chapters.
126--/
127-def sourceOf [Monad m] [MonadEnv m] [MonadError m] [MonadFileMap m]
128-    [MonadLiftT IO m] [MonadLiftT BaseIO m] (x : Name) : m String := do
129-  let some ranges ← findDeclarationRanges? x
130-    | throwError "no declaration range recorded for '{x}'"
131-  let env ← getEnv
132-  let text ←
133-    match env.getModuleIdxFor? x with
134-    | none => pure (← getFileMap)
135-    | some idx => do
136-      let modName := env.allImportedModuleNames[idx.toNat]!
137-      let sp ← getSrcSearchPath
138-      let some path ← sp.findModuleWithExt "lean" modName
139-        | throwError "source for module '{modName}' is not on the search path"
140-      pure (FileMap.ofString (← IO.FS.readFile path))
141-  return String.Pos.Raw.extract text.source
142-    (text.ofPosition ranges.range.pos) (text.ofPosition ranges.range.endPos)
143-
144-/-- The source text of a piece of syntax in the current file. -/
145-def sourceOfSyntax [Monad m] [MonadError m] [MonadFileMap m]
146-    (stx : Syntax) : m String := do
147-  let some r := stx.getRange?
148-    | throwErrorAt stx "no source range"
149-  return String.Pos.Raw.extract (← getFileMap).source r.start r.stop
150-
151-end
152-
153-end SFLCompat.Recall

1-module

4-
5-/-!
6-# Recall, checked byte for byte
7-
8-`sf_recall_source` lets a chapter restate a definition from earlier in the
9-development while the build checks that the restatement matches the
10-original's source text, byte for byte. The restated text is what the
11-reader already saw, and it can never drift from the original.
12-
13-```
14-sf_recall_source
15-  def twice (f : Nat → Nat) (n : Nat) : Nat := f (f n)
16-```
17-
18-The restated declaration is parsed but never elaborated; the check is
19-purely textual: after the block indentation is removed from each side, the
20-two texts must be equal, byte for byte. The restatement may sit at a
21-different indentation depth, but it may not be reflowed or respaced.
22-
23-The comparison covers whole declarations only. Carving a statement out of
24-the original's source would require parsing it, which is only possible in
25-the elaboration context of its declaration site; restating only a theorem
26-statement is therefore the province of `sf_recall statement`, which compares
27-elaborated types.
28--/
29-
30-namespace SFLCompat.Recall.Source
31-
32-open Lean Elab Command
33-
34-/--
35-`recall_source` restates a definition from earlier in the development and
36-checks that the restatement matches the original's source text, byte for
37-byte, modulo block indentation.
38--/
39-syntax (name := recallSrc) "sf_recall_source " command : command
40-
41-elab_rules : command
42-  | `(sf_recall_source $cmd:command) => do
43-    let decl ← declaredName cmd
44-    let x ← liftCoreM <| withoutExporting <|
45-      realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo decl.ident
46-    -- The restatement is never elaborated, so it produces no info of its
47-    -- own. The whole compared region is one big reference to the original:
48-    -- hovering anywhere in it shows the original, and go-to-definition
49-    -- jumps to it.
50-    addConstInfo cmd x
51-    let restated ← sourceOfSyntax cmd
52-    let original ← sourceOf x
53-    unless dedent restated == dedent original do
54-      throwErrorAt cmd
55-        (m!"the restatement of '{privateToUserName x}' does not match its source.\n\
56-            Original:{indentD original}\nRestated:{indentD restated}"
57-          ++ (← liftCoreM <| replaceWithOriginalHint cmd (dedent original) restated))
58-
